title: Independence of the K-injective resolution
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and $K\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Choose a cochain complex $C$ representing $K$, specified by an isomorphism $e:Q(C)\cong K$ in the derived category, and let $s:C\to I$ and $t:C\to J$ be K-injective resolutions of $C$ in the category of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$. Then every comparison $f:I\to J$ with $s\,f$ homotopic to $t$ induces an isomorphism of the derived-category images of the termwise global-sections map $\Gamma(T_{\Et},f)$ in $D(\Lambda)$; any two such comparisons induce the same morphism in $D(\Lambda)$. Consequently the object $\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)$ of [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] is independent, up to canonical isomorphism, of the chosen representative, resolutions, and comparisons.

proof.text: Choose a cochain representative $C$ of $K$, and write the two resolutions as $s:C\to I$ and $t:C\to J$. This is the meaning of the resolution notation in [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] and [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and let $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both $Q(s)$ and $Q(t)$ are invertible because $s,t$ are quasi-isomorphisms. A comparison $f:I\to J$ over $C$ (strictly or up to homotopy) therefore satisfies $Q(f)=Q(t)Q(s)^{-1}$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], lift $Q(s)Q(t)^{-1}:QJ\to QI$ to a homotopy class represented by $g:J\to I$. Since $I$ and $J$ are K-injective, injectivity of the same Hom bijection gives $[g f]=[1_I]$ and $[f g]=[1_J]$. Thus there are degree-minus-one families $h,k$ with $g f-1_I=d_Ih+hd_I$ and $f g-1_J=d_Jk+kd_J$. This proves that the given comparison, rather than just some map between $I$ and $J$, is a homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: Global sections are evaluation at the terminal object [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]; for $\Lambda$-module sheaves this evaluation has its inherited $\Lambda$-module structure and acts on maps by evaluation. It preserves sums, compositions and identities pointwise. Evaluating the identities from step 2 in each degree gives $\Gamma(g)\Gamma(f)-1=d\Gamma(h)+\Gamma(h)d$ and $\Gamma(f)\Gamma(g)-1=d\Gamma(k)+\Gamma(k)d$. Thus the two sections maps are inverse in the homotopy category of $\Lambda$-modules. Their images are inverse in $D(\Lambda)$, since the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] factors through the homotopy category. No exactness of sections is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, equivalence (1) and (3); the comparison and sections calculations are written out here

proof.text: The Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] also lifts $Q(t)Q(s)^{-1}$ to a comparison class $[f]$; injectivity with source $C$ and target $J$ gives $[f s]=[t]$. Any two comparisons over $C$ have this same image in $D(\mathcal A)$, hence are homotopic by injectivity with source $I$ and target $J$. The evaluated homotopy from step 3 shows that their sections maps agree in $D(\Lambda)$. For three resolutions $s_a:C\to I_a$, the comparison classes have derived images $Q(s_b)Q(s_a)^{-1}$, whose products satisfy $\alpha_{bc}\alpha_{ab}=\alpha_{ac}$ and $\alpha_{aa}=1$; injectivity gives these identities already in the homotopy category, hence after sections. For resolutions of possibly different cochain representatives, let $u_a:QI_a\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ be the specified identifications with $K$ (the representative identification composed with the inverse resolution map). Set $\beta_{ab}=u_b^{-1}u_a$. Surjectivity of the cited Hom bijection with source $I_a$ and K-injective target $I_b$ gives a class $[f_{ab}]$ with $Q([f_{ab}])=\beta_{ab}$, and injectivity makes this class unique. The equations $\beta_{bc}\beta_{ab}=u_c^{-1}u_bu_b^{-1}u_a=\beta_{ac}$ and $\beta_{aa}=1$ imply $[f_{bc}f_{ab}]=[f_{ac}]$ and $[f_{aa}]=[1]$ by injectivity. In particular $[f_{ba}]$ is inverse to $[f_{ab}]$. Evaluating the homotopies expressing these equations as in step 3 gives identity, inverse and cocycle equations for their sections maps in $D(\Lambda)$. These choice-independent, composable isomorphisms give precisely canonical independence of $\RGamma$ as defined in [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded].

citers.note: Uses the lemma only for the induced isomorphism after applying termwise global sections to K-injective comparisons; the corrected representative-level interface supplies this.
Uses the lemma as a tool to identify derived global-sections computations from K-injective resolutions; its bounded-below representative data remains compatible.

statement_change.what: The original prose binds K as an object of the derived category but then writes K→I and K→J as maps of cochain complexes. A K-injective resolution is a quasi-isomorphism from a representative cochain complex C, and a comparison is over C (or over K only after choosing an identification Q(C) ≅ K). The correction introduces C, the representative identification e, and maps s,t, while retaining the comparison, global-sections isomorphism, and canonical-independence clauses.
